stories.headline: Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 7 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
stories.summary: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
stories.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 7, which kicks off Thursday night with a game between the Patriots and Bears.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start advice, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday after 1 p.m. ET.

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

NE-CHI | PIT-NO | SF-ATL | CLE-TEN | IND-MIN | MIA-NYJ | TB-CAR

CIN-BAL | NYG-HOU | DEN-ARI | GB-DET | LAR-LV | KC-SEA | DAL-PHI

New England Patriots @ Chicago Bears
Projected score: Bears 26, Patriots 24

Lineup locks: Drake Maye, D'Andre Swift, A.J. Brown, Luther Burden III

Fantasy Scoop: Welcome back, Colston Loveland! After totaling 24.0 fantasy points during his first five games of the season, Loveland put up 18.5 points on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. His big game coincided with the triumphant return of Caleb Williams, who completed 30 out of 36 passes in the win. Loveland now leads all tight ends in snaps and is fifth in end zone targets (four), though he's way down in 21st place in receiving yards and has found the end zone just once.

Loveland's strong performance is enough to get him back into the weekly TE1 mix, but we shouldn't get too carried away, as he's hit 12.0 fantasy points only once this season and he had a total of just 3 yards on five targets during Weeks 1-2 (Williams was under center for most of that). Consider Loveland to be a mid-to-back-end TE1 against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one tight end (Brock Bowers) to reach 8.0 fantasy points this season.

Shadow Alert: This is far from a lock, but it's possible Christian Gonzalez shadows Rome Odunze, just like he has done for Garrett Wilson, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and DK Metcalf this season. Odunze aligns on the perimeter 77% of the time, which makes him the most likely candidate to see a lot of Gonzalez, though it's possible New England's top corner aligns at times against Burden (50% perimeter).

Over/under: 49.8 (5th highest)

Win probability: Bears 57% (13th highest)

Pittsburgh Steelers @ New Orleans Saints
Projected score: Steelers 29, Saints 20

Lineup locks: Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave, DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard

Fantasy Scoop: Bernard has graduated to "lineup lock" status following a terrific Week 6 effort in which he caught 11 out of 12 targets for 87 yards and one touchdown. This, after the rookie second-round pick posted a 6-80-0 receiving line on nine targets the week prior. Bernard's production is no fluke, as his route participation (85%) and target share (28%) have been outstanding during the span.

Bernard's short-area role (4.9 aDOT) may limit his explosive plays and scoring upside, but the high volume supplies him with a high floor, especially in PPR formats. It also helps his cause that Pittsburgh is the league's pass-heaviest team near the goal line (their 87% expected pass TD rate and 92% actual pass TD rate are both tops in the NFL). Consider Bernard to be a solid WR3 against a Saints defense that allowed 250 yards to New York Giants wide receivers last week.

Over/under: 49.7 (6th highest)

Win probability: Steelers 81% (3rd highest)

San Francisco 49ers @ Atlanta Falcons
Projected score: 49ers 29, Falcons 22

Lineup locks: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Bijan Robinson, Drake London, George Kittle

Fantasy Scoop: Right when it seemed like Kyle Pitts Sr. had fallen off the map (again), the most polarizing tight end in fantasy is back with a vengeance. After opening the 2026 season with a 2-20-0 receiving line on six targets through three games, Pitts improved to 3-47-0 on three targets in Week 4, 5-42-1 on six targets in Week 5 and 5-60-2 on seven targets in Week 6. Although Pitts' route participation has been volatile this season, it has steadied over the past two weeks -- and he also played on a season-high 76% of Atlanta's snaps last Sunday.

Pitts' usage isn't quite as high as it was last season, but as long as his connection with Michael Penix Jr. remains strong, there's enough here to get him back into the weekly TE1 discussion. Of course, we need to downgrade him here in Week 7, as the 49ers have allowed zero touchdowns and the fourth-fewest fantasy points to tight ends this season. Only Trey McBride and Chig Okonkwo have cleared 5.0 points against them.

Over/under: 50.7 (4th highest)

Win probability: 49ers 73% (4th highest)

Cleveland Browns @ Tennessee Titans
Projected score: Browns 17, Titans 16

Lineup locks: Denzel Boston, Carnell Tate

Fantasy Scoop: With Quinshon Judkins sidelined in Week 5, Jaleel McLaughlin led the Cleveland backfield, playing on 37 snaps, carrying the ball nine times for 41 yards and adding 14 yards on four targets. Audric Estime (18 snaps) was also involved and, while he wasn't targeted and was held to 19 yards on nine carries, he did score the team's lone rushing touchdown.

If Judkins returns in Week 7, both McLaughlin and Estime should be on waivers. If Judkins remains out, neither replacement back will be a recommended flex against a solid Titans run defense, though McLaughlin's passing-game work gives him a slight edge if you're in a tough spot. Note that, should Dylan Sampson return from IR and Judkins remain out, it's Sampson who would be the preferred (albeit still uninspiring) flex from this backfield.

Over/under: 32.6 (Lowest)

Win probability: Browns 55% (Lowest)

Indianapolis Colts @ Minnesota Vikings
Projected score: Vikings 26, Colts 16

Lineup locks: Jonathan Taylor, Justin Jefferson

Fantasy Scoop: Keenan Allen set season-high marks in targets (11), receptions (eight) and yardage (82) against the Titans on Sunday. Allen has now handled at least nine targets in all three games since Alec Pierce was placed on IR. The heavy usage has helped him to a respectable 14.7 fantasy points per game, which includes 16-plus points in two of the three outings.

Allen's short-area role (7.9 aDOT) in the Colts' struggling offense will limit his scoring opportunities (one end zone target this season), but the 25% target share he's enjoyed over the last three games is plenty to keep him in the WR3/flex discussion, especially if Tyler Warren remains sidelined.

Of course, we need to downgrade this entire passing game in Week 7 against a Vikings defense that has allowed the third-fewest passing yards and only three passing TDs this season. Minnesota hasn't allowed any wide receivers to clear 12.0 fantasy points in a game since Week 1.

Over/under: 41.9 (12th highest)

Win probability: Vikings 84% (Highest)

Miami Dolphins @ New York Jets
Projected score: Jets 24, Dolphins 14

Lineup locks: Breece Hall, Garrett Wilson

Fantasy Scoop: Omar Cooper Jr. returned from injury on Sunday and made a major impact. The first-round rookie played on 82% of offensive snaps and posted a 6-103-1 receiving line on seven targets. The big game was a surprise after Cooper missed Weeks 2-5 due to a high ankle sprain suffered on the fourth snap of his pro career back in Week 1. It was a positive sign that Cooper immediately leapfrogged Tim Patrick and Isaiah Williams on the depth chart, but it's also notable that Adonai Mitchell was sidelined and Wilson was dealing with shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.

Cooper should be on rosters, but he should be considered for a flex spot only if Mitchell remains out this week. Target volume is likely to be at a premium against a struggling Miami team that has faced the fewest WR targets and thus allowed the third-fewest WR fantasy points this season. In five games, only three receivers have reached double-digit fantasy points against Miami -- and none have reached 20.

Over/under: 38.6 (13th highest)

Win probability: Jets 82% (2nd highest)

Tampa Bay Buccaneers @ Carolina Panthers
Projected score: Panthers 24, Buccaneers 21

Lineup locks: Bucky Irving, Chuba Hubbard, Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Emeka Egbuka

Fantasy Scoop: After producing 52 yards and one touchdown on seven touches in Week 5, Egbuka followed that up with 48 yards and one touchdown on seven touches in Week 6. Egbuka's fantasy point totals in the two games (17.2 and 17.8) are a significant step forward after he had failed to reach 12.0 points in any of his prior 12 games.

Egbuka's target volume has been very good -- a 26% share on the season that includes a career-high 16 targets against Pittsburgh on Sunday. Of course, that heavy usage came with Jalon Daniels under center, and Baker Mayfield may return in Week 7. In his three games with Mayfield this season, Egbuka averaged 6.7 targets and 10.9 fantasy PPG.

The Panthers have been solid against receivers this season, though both starting corners remain sidelined and DeVonta Smith just nailed them for 7-75-1 on Sunday. Regardless of which QB is under center, Egbuka has found his way back into the WR2/3 mix.

Over/under: 44.7 (10th highest)

Win probability: Panthers 60% (8th highest)

Cincinnati Bengals @ Baltimore Ravens
Projected score: Bengals 24, Ravens 22

Lineup locks: Joe Burrow, Derrick Henry, Chase Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Zay Flowers, Tee Higgins

Shadow Report: DJ Turner is a strong bet to shadow Flowers when he aligns on the perimeter, which he has done on 45% of his routes this season. Turner has emerged as one of the league's top shadow corners, having already traveled with Emeka Egbuka (11.3 fantasy points in the game), Xavier Hutchinson (6.7), DK Metcalf (12.1), Parker Washington (2.0) and Chris Bell (2.6) this season.

Turner also shadowed 14 times last season (those receivers averaged 8.8 fantasy PPG), two of which came against Flowers. Flowers was held to a 2-6-0 receiving line on seven targets in the Week 13 matchup, but was better with a 3-68-1 line on five targets in Week 15. Flowers will avoid Turner on roughly half of his routes, but note that the Bengals have allowed a 56% completion rate to receivers (fourth lowest) and none have cleared 15.0 points in a game. Flowers remains a lineup lock, but a down game wouldn't be a shock.

Over/under: 45.9 (9th highest)

Win probability: Bengals 57% (12th highest)

New York Giants @ Houston Texans
Projected score: Texans 30, Giants 24

Lineup locks: C.J. Stroud, Nico Collins, Malik Nabers, Isaiah Likely

Fantasy Scoop: Jaylin Noel caught all four targets for a career-high 107 yards and one touchdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6. Despite the strong game (and despite the fact that he also found the end zone in Week 5), Noel is not yet a viable flex option. The 2025 third-round pick remains a situational player, having yet to eclipse 60% route participation or a 16% target share in any single game of his career.

Noel is trending toward locking down Houston's primary slot receiver job, but that's unlikely to lead to consistent production with so many mouths to feed at wide receiver in that huddle. That list includes Marvin Harrison Jr. (four targets on 11 snaps in his Houston debut), whose role will continue to expand, as well as a now-healthy Tank Dell. At best, Noel is a speculative bench stash, but there's not much upside in the short term.

Over/under: 54.4 (3rd highest)

Win probability: Texans 71% (5th highest)

Denver Broncos @ Arizona Cardinals
Projected score: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21

Lineup locks: Michael Wilson, Trey McBride

Fantasy Scoop: Wilson is a tricky evaluation after a very volatile start to the season. Arizona's top receiver appeared to be primed for a huge season after posting 11-89-1 and 7-95-0 receiving lines on a combined 30 targets during Weeks 3-4. However, he's seen exactly seven targets in his other four games, none of which resulted in more than 10.6 fantasy points. That includes a pair of duds since Harrison's departure, a 4-30-0 showing in an elite matchup against Detroit in Week 5 and a 4-32-0 line against the Trent McDuffie-less Rams last week.

Although the production has been inconsistent, Wilson checks a lot of boxes, including ranking no lower than eighth among receivers in snaps, routes, target share, targets, end zone targets and air yards. As long as that keeps up, he'll find his way to plenty of big games. Wilson is a WR3 against Denver, though you should note that he'll be a candidate for shadow coverage from Pat Surtain II if the standout corner returns from injury.

Over/under: 44.7 (11th highest)

Win probability: Broncos 61% (7th highest)

Green Bay Packers @ Detroit Lions
Projected score: Lions 30, Packers 28

Lineup locks: Jordan Love, Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Sam LaPorta, Tucker Kraft

Fantasy Scoop: When we last saw the Lions in action (Week 5), Jameson Williams scored his only two touchdowns of the season during a 45-21 win over Arizona. It was Williams' second-consecutive game with 16-plus fantasy points after he fell short of 9.0 points in each of his first three games of the season. The good news is that Williams' playing time has been excellent (89% route participation), but the concern is that his targets have been extremely volatile. He's reached eight targets twice but has seen exactly four targets in the other three games (including the two-TD outing).

Williams' 15.4% target share is his lowest since 2023 and will need to increase in order to allow consistent fantasy production. The speedy receiver should be viewed as a WR3 this week against a Green Bay defense that sits middle of the pack in WR fantasy points allowed.

Over/under: 58.2 (Highest)

Win probability: Lions 60% (9th highest)

Los Angeles Rams @ Las Vegas Raiders
Projected score: Rams 29, Raiders 26

Lineup locks: Matthew Stafford, Kyren Williams, Ashton Jeanty, Puka Nacua, Brock Bowers

Fantasy Scoop: Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to miss 6-10 weeks of action, which will free up roughly 20% of the Rams' targets and, perhaps more notably, a large chunk of the team's opportunities near the goal line as Adams has scored four touchdowns and is responsible for five of the team's nine end zone targets this season. Adams' absence figures to lead to even more reliance on Nacua, but it's possible the rest of usage is spread around to the team's depth receivers and tight ends.

Konata Mumpfield is the next man up at receiver, but he managed only one good game while filling in for Adams during Weeks 16-18 last season (a 14-5-50-0 receiving line) and for Nacua during Weeks 2-3 this season (1-12-0 in Week 2, but 4-93-1 in Week 3). At best, Mumpfield is a speculative bench stash this weekend. TE duo Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee are now better bets to find the end zone, but the two share so much work that they don't make for viable fantasy starters either. Instead, keep Terrance Ferguson stashed on IR, as he could find his way into the TE1 mix if he's able to return in the near future.

Over/under: 55.3 (2nd highest)

Win probability: Rams 59% (10th highest)

Kansas City Chiefs @ Seattle Seahawks
Projected score: Chiefs 25, Seahawks 22

Lineup locks: Kenneth Walker III, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Xavier Worthy

Fantasy Scoop: After opening the season with 21.7 and 29.0 fantasy point efforts, Patrick Mahomes has faded to 15.9, 17.0 and 10.5 during his last three outings. Mahomes continues to play well, but the game script hasn't allowed much passing (no more than 30 passing attempts in four out of five games) and he hasn't added much with his legs (after posting a 7-23-1 rushing line in Week 1, he's totaled a 10-34-0 line over his last four games).

With Walker playing at an elite level, Kansas City has run a balanced offense (Andy Reid generally leans very pass-heavy) and has run the ball often near the goal line (56% of Chiefs touchdowns have been passes this year, compared to 69% during the prior Mahomes era). This week, Mahomes will face off with a Seattle defense that has allowed the fewest passing yards, lowest YPA (5.3) and second-fewest QB fantasy points this season. Seattle has held four of their opposing six QBs below 10.0 fantasy points.

Mahomes is a fringe fantasy starter most weeks but should absolutely be on benches against Seattle's elite defense.

Over/under: 47.2 (8th highest)

Win probability: Chiefs 58% (11th highest)

Dallas Cowboys @ Philadelphia Eagles
Projected score: Cowboys 26, Eagles 21

Lineup locks: Javonte Williams, Saquon Barkley, CeeDee Lamb, DeVonta Smith, George Pickens

Fantasy Scoop: Tanner McKee made his first start in place of Jalen Hurts (IR) last week and it certainly could have gone worse from a fantasy perspective. The 2023 sixth-round pick was inefficient (4.8 YPA, 58.0 C%) but attempted 45 passes, which allowed a strong fantasy showing from Smith (7-75-1 on 14 targets) and a solid outing from Dallas Goedert (6-61-0 on eight targets).

McKee was competent enough that we can feel secure with keeping Smith as a lineup lock against a Dallas defense that has allowed the third-highest EPA against the pass, as well as the seventh-most fantasy points to receivers. Goedert, meanwhile, has managed 12 catches on 17 targets over the two games since his return from injury and remains a back-end TE1.

Over/under: 47.2 (7th highest)

Win probability: Cowboys 65% (6th highest)

stories.headline: Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win
stories.summary: Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas said he regrets telling his players to ease off towards the end of their famous 4-1 win against misfiring Manchester United.
stories.body:
Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas said he regrets telling his players to ease off towards the end of their famous 4-1 win against misfiring Manchester United.

The Champions League upstarts heaped pressure on Red Devils boss Michael Carrick by swatting aside the three-time European champions with ease on Wednesday evening.

Nico Paz marked a sparkling man-of-the-match display with a brace at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, where Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramón also struck for the ever-improving Serie A side.

But Fàbregas' pride in the performance was tinged by disappointment at seeing United substitute Joshua Zirkzee score a stoppage-time consolation, admitting he turned his attention to Saturday's match against Sassuolo during the closing stages.

"I believe that tactically speaking the team played a rather good game," the former Arsenal and Chelsea star said.

"I regret maybe the last 10 minutes when I was the one telling the team to slow down the pace because there was another game and maybe with a 4-0 lead they could have managed something.

"I told Tasos Douvikas not to run anymore, to stay in the middle and maybe that is what I regret, because I'm the first one who always pushes the fight until the end. That goal hurt me."

stories.headline: Angel Reese keeps Dream rolling with Game 3 win over Valkyries in WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Angel Reese kept the Dream rolling in Game 3 with a 97-71 win as Atlanta took a 2-1 lead over the Valkyries in the WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- Angel Reese continued to bark at anyone in her vicinity -- the opponent, her teammates, even the officials -- during Wednesday night's Game 3 of the WNBA Finals. At one point, she even took a moment to celebrate with six-time All-Star Alyssa Thomas, who was sitting courtside.

Reese explained her mentality in simple terms after leading the Dream to a 97-71 win over the Valkyries that put Atlanta two wins away from its first WNBA championship.

"Y'all not taking this from us, and that's in my heart," Reese said. "Like, I'm not letting you take this from us. I think [that confidence] becomes contagious within the team. They feel that confidence too."

Reese, a three-time All-Star, has fully evolved into the emotional leader of the Dream, who took a 2-1 lead in the Finals. In the process, she continued to set league records, as she finished with 21 points and 12 rebounds, making her the youngest player in Finals history to record three straight double-doubles and joining A'ja Wilson as the only players to record 20 points and 10 rebounds in consecutive Finals games.

A sold-out crowd of 17,099 had State Farm Arena rocking as Atlanta finally found its offense after a pair of low-scoring affairs in San Francisco.

"I knew it was coming, especially back home," Reese said of Wednesday's offensive output. "It feels good to be home on your own court and you've seen the basket that you shoot on every single day. ... Everybody contributed from top to bottom.

"And when you shoot 49%, I mean, you win games."

The Dream shot a series-high 49.3% from the field and knocked down nine 3-pointers, their most of these Finals. Rhyne Howard found her flow with 16 points, four assists and four rebounds while becoming the first player in WNBA history to record five steals in consecutive Finals games. Naz Hillmon added 15 points, DeWanna Bonner put up 12 off the bench, and Jordin Canada finished with 10 points, eight assists and six rebounds.

It was just the third time in the 2026 playoffs that a team shot better than 45% from the field against the Valkyries.

"We definitely showed that we played a little more free tonight, and we got easier looks because of it," Howard said. "We weren't stressed. We just let the game come to us, and we went out and we won.

"Our attention to detail, our spacing, making sure that we're moving, giving people the lanes to drive the ball, finding each other for open shots. We were more together on that end of the floor. ... We were just feeding off of each other."

The Valkyries continued to turn the ball over at an alarming rate, committing 17 turnovers Wednesday night that the Dream turned into 22 points. Golden State had 18 turnovers in the Game 2 loss.

Points also continued to be hard to come by for Golden State, which shot 34.8% from the floor. Gabby Williams scored a team-high 15, and Cecilia Zandalasini and Janelle Salaun tallied 13 apiece. (That was a playoff high for Salaun after her postseason minutes had been reduced.) Tiffany Hayes kept the team in the game early and finished with 14 points off the bench.

"I think this game, they wanted it more than us, and that's not who we are," Hayes said. "That's not who we've been, and that's not how we got here. [The turnovers are] a lot of us being undisciplined. ... Uncharacteristic of us."

Before Wednesday's contest, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said there was nothing she liked about Game 2 and was insistent that her team was ready to fight.

"Sometimes, promises aren't kept," she said afterward. "I think there's sometimes individual punches and some people with great spurts and some people with great energy. But it's like, well, then how can we do it all together?

"The will is there, the want to is there, but the fight together, I'm missing -- the piece of putting it together."

stories.headline: Ranking top players in Brewers-Rays World Series
stories.summary: Here's how the rosters of the Rays and the Brewers stack up and who is primed to do the most jaw-dropping things on baseball's biggest stage.
stories.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays were each the top team in their respective league during the regular season -- and that level of talent is reflected on their postseason rosters.

As the two No. 1 seeds prepare to meet in the World Series, we break down the best of the best on both clubs by ranking all 52 expected participants based on how good I think they'll be in the Series and predicting who will take home some superlatives by the time the dust settles.

Let's dig into the stars in a World Series featuring the hardest-throwing ace on the planet and some of the most electric young position players in the sport.

Jump to: Rankings | Superlatives

Ranking every player in the World Series

1. Jacob Misiorowski, SP, Brewers

What else can I say other than to (1) watch him pitch if you somehow haven't yet, and (2) if you haven't, also head over to his Baseball Savant page and see it bleeding with red in every category because he is so elite that analytical scales can't contain him.

He throws harder than any other starter in baseball (averaging 100.6 mph, behind only Mason Miller), his cutter sits in the mid-90s and his curveball sneaks into the 90s -- which helps explain why all of his pitches are plus. His extension, velocity and shape all make his fastball the best pitch in baseball, so it's not surprising it had the highest run value in baseball. Misiorowski could appear three times in the Series and is my pick to win MVP.

2. Junior Caminero, 3B, Rays

Caminero is an easy player for a casual fan to scout: He is an electric factory at the plate due to both incredible bat speed and a tendency to chase out of the zone. He's second in baseball in home runs over the past two seasons (87), behind only Kyle Schwarber, and is a threat to take over any game with every swing.

3. Drew Rasmussen, SP, Rays

Rasmussen has been underappreciated for years due to lack of prospect track record and durability/injury issues, but he has blossomed into one of the best pitchers in the game this year.

Tampa Bay's ace has four above-average pitches and above-average command, and he could really impact the Series with potentially three starts -- or two starts and a relief appearance.

4. Brice Turang, 2B, Brewers

Turang isn't as flashy as Misiorowski or Caminero but has quietly turned into one of the best players in baseball after showing that potential early in his high school career.

Turang has a strong batting eye along with above-average power, speed and defense, all of which helped him post a 5.9 WAR this season.

5. Jackson Chourio, LF, Brewers

Chourio has been consistent and durable since showing up in the big leagues with an $82 million extension at 20 years old.

He is above-average at all five traditional tools, and curtailing his chase rate a bit could make him one of the best players in the sport.

6. William Contreras, C, Brewers

Contreras is a fine defender but a standout hitter, similar at the same stage to his older brother, Willson.

William has regularly posted .350+ on-base percentages and 20 or so homers every season, which is truly elite for an every-day catcher.

7. Garrett Mitchell, CF, Brewers

Mitchell has elite speed, arm strength, defensive ability and bat speed. He has had trouble staying healthy in the past, but not this season; so now, his swing-and-miss is the thing holding back his tools from making him an even better player.

8. Jake Bauers, 1B, Brewers

Bauers is journeyman who, like Andrew Vaughn below, has found himself with the Brewers. There's some swing-and-miss to his game, and he doesn't offer a ton of defensive value, but he can hit and has been hot this postseason.

9. Freddy Peralta, SP, Rays

The Rays acquired Peralta at the deadline and spiked his changeup usage while lowering his slider usage, which altered his approach against right-handed hitters a good bit. His peripherals dropped at least a half-run while his ERA dropped almost two full runs. And he has been good in the playoffs too, which is great timing as he is set to hit the free agent market after the season.

10. Cooper Pratt, SS, Brewers

Pratt was a longtime top-100 prospect who debuted this season after landing a $50.75 million extension. He is a solid shortstop defender and a plus runner who contributes in all phases while offering a league-average performance at the plate.

11. Yandy Diaz, DH, Rays

Diaz has been a consistent power source for the Rays over the years due to his strong bat control and huge exit velos, despite a flat swing plane that produces a lot of ground balls too.

12. Logan Henderson, SP, Brewers

He is a former top-100 prospect who had a strong rookie year this season and is now the Brewers' No. 2 starter by throwing over 80% fastballs and changeups, tunneled to the top and bottom of the zone.

13. Jonathan Aranda, 1B, Rays

He has a strong eye at the plate and above-average power, and he is a solid defender at first base. Above-average regulars such as Aranda at the league minimum are a key part of the team-building philosophy of both these teams.

14. Trevor Megill, RP, Brewers

Megill posted the sixth-best reliever WAR in baseball this year, relying on a triple-digit fastball and a power curveball that he often buries just below the zone.

15. Victor Mesa Jr., RF, Rays

He had a breakout 2026 campaign as a strong runner and fielder who registered career-high power numbers this season.

16. Robert Gasser, SP, Brewers

Gasser is a solid No. 4 starter type due to a deep five-pitch mix, strong command and a good fastball shape created by elite extension.

17. Aaron Ashby, RP, Brewers

He gets above-average whiff and ground ball rates from the left side with a sinker that's up to 100 mph and a mid-80s slurve.

18. Liam Hicks, C, Rays

Hicks is a solid defender with enough offensive upside to play some first base or DH to keep his bat in the lineup after a breakthrough 2026 season.

19. Jonny DeLuca, CF, Rays

DeLuca is an elite defender, runner and thrower with above-average bat speed, but his bat control and pitch selection undercut those tools a bit.

20. Nick Martinez, SP, Rays

Martinez threw 180.0 innings with a 3.10 ERA, but his below-average strikeout rate makes him more valuable in the regular season than in the high-octane-stuff environment of the playoffs.

21. Joey Ortiz, SS, Brewers

He is an elite defender with decent offensive upside and defensive versatility.

22. Dustin May, SP, Brewers

May has absurd spin rates and movement on his breaking stuff along with two distinct fastball shapes, but his command and not getting elite whiff rates from that strong stuff have been limitations.

23. Chandler Simpson, LF, Rays

Simpson is a throwback outfielder whose whole game is built around his elite acceleration and plus-plus long speed. He has bottom-of-the-scale power but makes tons of contact.

24. Bryan Baker, RP, Rays

Baker has grown into one of the better relievers in baseball, with a cutter shape to his 95 to 98 mph fastball and a changeup that he tunnels well with the heater, to the top and bottom of the zone, respectively.

25. Kevin Kelly, RP, Rays

Kelly is a true sidearmer and throws mostly sinker/changeup to the bottom of the zone from that low slot. That seems simple, but the angles coupled with 92 to 95 mph velocity give hitters fits.

26. Abner Uribe, RP, Brewers

Uribe is an old-school power reliever who relies on a sinker and a sweeper to great effect after his command took a step forward last season.

27. Tyler Wells, RP, Rays

Wells throws from a high arm slot with a cutter shape to his fastball and a few variants of that pitch. That unique approach helps make his changeup very effective.

28. Richie Palacios, 2B, Rays

Palacios is a solid regular who fits for Tampa Bay as the primary second basemen versus right-handed pitchers.

29. Andrew Vaughn, 1B, Brewers

The No. 3 pick in the 2019 draft was a bust with the White Sox until finding himself with Milwaukee last season. He is now a solid regular who is mostly just facing left-handed pitching for the Brewers.

30. Griffin Jax, SP, Rays

Jax can pitch in multiple roles after strictly being a reliever with the Twins, and his outings are helped by a deep pitch mix.

31. Ryan Vilade, LF, Rays

Vilade has big tools -- elite bat speed and sprint speed with a plus arm -- along with defensive versatility, and he enjoyed a career year at the plate leaning into the pull/lift elements of his swing.

He is a higher-upside platoon batter who should play when Robert Gasser starts or come in as a pinch hitter to face the many lefties in the Brewers' bullpen.

32. David Hamilton, 3B, Brewers

He is an elite runner and a passable infield defender with a small-ball-based offensive approach who is on a bit of a heater in the postseason.

33. Cam Booser, RP, Rays

Booser found his command this year with Tampa Bay like many pitchers before him have. His mid-90s fastball works at the top of the zone, and his slider tunnels with it to the bottom of the zone.

34. Ian Seymour, RP, Rays

Seymour threw 132⅔ innings with strong peripherals across multiple roles this season, but he has been moved to relief for the playoffs. His fastball/changeup combination works in any role despite fringy fastball velocity at 90 to 93 mph.

35. DL Hall, RP, Brewers

Hall's command has been a bugaboo since he was a first-round pick in 2017, but he is still relied on by the Brewers because his stuff is above average, headlined by a mid-90s sinker and standout breaking pitches.

36. JoJo Romero, RP, Brewers

The Brewers paid a high prospect amount to acquire Romero at the deadline from St. Louis, and his strike-throwing capability has been markedly better since coming to Milwaukee. He has been relying even more on his grounder-producing sinker as a Brewer.

37. Taylor Walls, SS, Rays

Walls has a very light offensive impact but is a strong baserunner and a steady defender playing every day at shortstop.

38. Antonio Senzatela, RP, Brewers

Senzatela is a longtime starter who transitioned to relief this season at age 31 with a velo spike up to 97.3 mph on average.

39. Cedric Mullins, CF, Rays

Mullins has great defensive instincts and above-average speed, but he struggled hitting for average this season, so he is a reserve now.

40. Gary Sanchez, C, Brewers

He is an offensive-oriented backup catcher with big arm strength, but he has only one plate appearance in the postseason so far.

41. Shane Drohan, RP, Brewers

Drohan made his MLB debut this year at age 27 and was an effective innings-eater and long reliever, but he has been pushed down the depth chart to long relief/opener in the playoffs.

42. Ben Williamson, 3B, Rays

Williamson is a versatile, standout infield defender with limited offensive upside who is the right-handed side of a platoon with Richie Palacios.

43. Christian Yelich, DH, Brewers

Yelich is well past his best years, hitting .235 with 12 homers in 118 games played this season, but he is still a useful veteran bat as the left-handed side of a DH platoon.

44. Sal Frelick, RF, Brewers

Frelick is the left-handed-hitting side of a right-field platoon but hasn't hit much this year, mostly offering contact, speed, baserunning and defensive versatility at 5-foot-9.

45. Luis Lara, CF, Brewers

Lara became a top-100 prospect this season in a breakout year at Triple-A, but he hasn't hit nearly as much in the big leagues or the playoffs (aside from a huge hit against Tarik Skubal in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series) while now platooning with Sal Frelick in right field.

46. Kyle Harrison, RP, Brewers

Harrison was a breakout candidate as a starter early this season who regressed heavily in the second half and moved to the bullpen in September.

47. Nick Fortes, C, Rays

Fortes is a solid backup catcher with defensive chops and is good enough with the bat to not be an offensive drain.

48. Cole Sulser, RP, Rays

Sulser throws his fastball and changeup over 80% of the time and has a reverse split, performing better against lefties than righties.

49. Steven Matz, RP, Rays

Matz is making the fourth-highest salary on the Rays and has become a long reliever. He is an effective veteran lefty but has been just OK this season.

50. Chad Patrick, RP, Brewers

Patrick was a really solid long reliever all season, though now some starters such as Kyle Harrison have moved to the pen for the playoffs and are ahead of Patrick in the pecking order.

51. Brody Hopkins, RP, Rays

Hopkins has some of the best raw stuff on Earth but hasn't appeared in the playoffs yet after walking nearly a batter per inning in both the big leagues and Triple-A this season. He might not pitch at all in the World Series but could be electric if he does.

52. Jorge Mateo, SS, Rays

Mateo is the Rays' utility infielder and is being used as a pinch runner and a defensive replacement.

World Series superlatives

Fastest pitch of the World Series will be thrown by: Misiorowski

You could've guessed this one without doing much research, as Misiorowski has the second-highest average fastball velo in the sport, which is truly incredible for a starting pitcher.

The Brewers have most of the elite velocity arms in the Series, with Uribe, Ashby and Megill all in the mix here.

Best breaking pitch will be: Megill's curveball

Megill relies on two pitches: a 96 to 100 mph fastball in the zone and an 86 to 90 mph power curveball (or the "deathball" variant, as some call it) mostly below the zone.

The others under consideration: Misiorowski's cutter/slider, Rasmussen's cutter/slider, Uribe's slider, Drohan's slider and Jax's sweeper.

Best changeup/splitter will be from: Wells

Henderson's offering is the only one of note on the Brewers, while the Rays have about a half dozen of note, with Seymour, Martinez, Baker, Kelly and Rasmussen all in the mix.

Hardest hit ball in play will be hit by: Caminero

This one was pretty easy, as Caminero would be the pick of any casual fan who simply watched these teams play and didn't know about exit velos. Mitchell, Bauers, Chourio and Diaz are in the next tier.

Highest sprint speed will be recorded by: Simpson

This one is quite close, as Simpson's top-end speed is rivaled by that of Mitchell, Hamilton, Mateo and DeLuca. But the Rays outfielder gets the nod here because his first step and acceleration are truly elite, and Simpson's whole game is organized around his speed.

Best defender will be: Turang

Some platoon/bench players (including Mullins and Ortiz) are candidates with limited playing time, while Chourio and DeLuca are the other regulars with a strong case.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Previews, stats and betting intel for Thursday's dozen games
stories.summary: Get your multi-view ready, hockey fans, it's another busy night!
stories.body:
Regular readers of NHL Tonight know that with it being Thursday there will be a lot of hockey games tonight.

Indeed, with a dozen contests, it's yet another night where it pays to have Power Play on ESPN+, along with a heavy dose of the multi-view option.

Here's a look at what you need to know for each of tonight's 12 contests, including betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Nashville Predators at Boston Bruins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BOS -155, O/U: 5.5

There's another new format for the All-Star Game this season -- a round-robin, 3-on-3 tournament with teams composed of players based on nationality. Various players skating in this game could be on the ice in February for that event, including American Olympians Jeremy Swayman and Charlie McAvoy, with Czechia native David Pastrnak joining Team Rest of World.

Is there a case for Steven Stamkos to make Team Canada? The future Hall of Famer has 10 points through eight games, after netting 42 goals last season.

New York Rangers at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYR -112, O/U: 6.5

If the season was over right now, these are two playoff teams! There are more than 70 games remaining on each team's calendar so let's not draw up the parade routes just yet, but it's notable for the fact that neither was close to a playoff berth in 2025-26.

The Rangers have been the beneficiary of a breakout performance by Dylan Garand, while the Leafs have been paced (unsurprisingly) by Auston Matthews and William Nylander, along with newcomer Kirill Marchenko and 21-year-old Easton Cowan. Who earns the valuable two points out of this one?

San Jose Sharks at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -130, O/U: 6.5

Two of the biggest trades this summer included the Senators: the trade sending Brady Tkachuk to Florida, and the subsequent deal to land Sharks winger William Eklund (using the No. 9 pick from the Panthers in that swap). The Sens were reunited with Brady on Wednesday, but the Sharks will not get to see their old pal William on the ice on Thursday -- he's out several more weeks after ankle surgery.

Nevertheless, the healthy Senators will hope to slow down a potent Sharks attack that knocked off the Canadiens earlier this week.

Anaheim Ducks at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -198, O/U: 6.5

To some degree, both of these teams were expected to be in the playoff picture by season's end. To do that, they'll both need to start stringing wins together. The Ducks went oh-fer on their other stops in the NYC metro area, extending their current losing streak to four games.

The Devils have had some impressive wins lately (4-3 over the Avs, 7-1 against the Rangers), but have also been on the wrong side of lopsided losses to the Sens, Mammoth and Islanders.

Florida Panthers at Pittsburgh Penguins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -105, O/U: 6.5

If nothing else, Penguins games have been exciting this season. Pittsburgh is scoring 3.30 goals per game, and allowing 3.80; that's fun for everyone! Florida will be playing this game 24 hours after the emotional high of taking on Brady Tkachuk's former teammates in Ottawa. Can they summon a second wind against Sidney Crosby & Co.?

Los Angeles Kings at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | NYI -120, O/U: 5.5

It took seven games, but the Kings are finally on the board with a victory in 2026-27! The defiant 5-2 win was emblematic of what they haven't done much of this season: scoring goals (with just 12 total in the six prior games).

That newfound offense will be put to the test against one of the game's finest netminders, Ilya Sorokin, who is fourth this season in both goals-against average (1.72) and save percentage (.934).

Vegas Golden Knights at St. Louis Blues

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -120, O/U: 6.5

Speaking of scoring, the Golden Knights have two players on the Top-10 scoring leaderboard at this juncture -- Jack Eichel and Mark Stone -- both of whom are on pace to finish with career highs in points.

Standing in their way is Blues goalie Joel Hofer, who got back on track with a 32-save win against Winnipeg on Tuesday following a five-goals-against loss to the Wild.

Winnipeg Jets at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -205, O/U: 5.5

Prior to the trade request/holdout/suspension of Connor Hellebuyck, this game had shaped up to be a showdown between two of the top American goalies of this generation, with Jake Oettinger manning the crease for the Stars.

Regardless, there are still two very important points on the line for both the Stars -- who come in on a three-game heater -- and the Jets -- who have lost three straight after a better-than-expected start.

Minnesota Wild at Calgary Flames

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -192, O/U: 5.5

On paper, this one doesn't look too close. But on some nights, the Flames look like they can play with -- and beat -- just about anyone. To wit, their recent wins over the Hurricanes and Ducks.

Or, it could turn out like losses to Colorado (7-3) or Vegas (6-2).

Carolina Hurricanes at Edmonton Oilers

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -115, O/U: 6.5

A potential Stanley Cup Final preview? This matchup has a 2.51% chance of occurring, per Stathletes projections. And while those who like "big markets" to be on the biggest stage, there is no shortage of star power in this matchup.

Edmonton's Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard -- along with Carolina's Sebastian Aho -- are all among the top point scorers this season.

Utah Mammoth at Seattle Kraken

10 p.m. ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | UTA -162, O/U: 6.5

It might be surprising for some to see the Mammoth atop the mighty Central Division standings after 10 games, although their inspired postseason appearance was a clue that something big is being built in Utah.

But the Kraken's hold on the No. 3 spot in the Pacific? That qualifies as a legitimate shock, given what the franchise had done in recent seasons. This contest will be an important one for both teams to continue building their identity as legit contenders in the West.

Detroit Red Wings at Vancouver Canucks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DET -170, O/U: 6.5

After winning two of their first three games this season, the Canucks have regressed back to essentially where many believed they'd be, and lost their next eight.

The Red Wings are trending in the opposite direction, with at least one point in each of their past five (two wins, and three OT/SO losses). Do both trends continue on Thursday?
