stories.headline: Christian Horner to Mercedes? Ex-Red Bull boss reveals pre-Toto Wolff approach
stories.summary: Christian Horner has revealed he rejected an offer to become Mercedes' Formula 1 team principal in 2012, before the team appointed his future rival Toto Wolff.
stories.body:
Christian Horner has revealed he rejected an offer to become Mercedes' Formula 1 team principal in 2012, before the team appointed his future rival Toto Wolff.

Horner claims in his new autobiography, Drive, that F1 legend and Mercedes' new non-executive chairman Niki Lauda -- with whom he had previously discussed Lewis Hamilton's future -- visited his home during the off-season and offered him a substantial salary to leave Red Bull.

The former Red Bull boss says he turned down the opportunity out of loyalty to the team he had helped build, with Mercedes subsequently embarking on a period of dominance under Wolff and Hamilton.

"Maybe our interactions over Lewis had stuck with him because later that year, during the Christmas break, Niki came to my house and asked me to join Mercedes as his team principal," Horner wrote.

"I was caught off guard. Leaving Red Bull had never crossed my mind. When he then laid out a series of dazzling numbers, I realized he was discussing my potential salary.

"'Red Bull will never pay you what Mercedes can,' he said. 'I respect you as a racer. I want you to come. Besides, Helmut [Marko, Red Bull adviser] is a miserable b------.'"

The approach came after Horner had held discussions with Lauda about Hamilton's future, with the British driver considering leaving McLaren at the end of the 2012 season. Hamilton held ultimately unfruitful talks with Red Bull due to the finances involved, but Horner knew Lauda and Mercedes would be interested.

Indeed, Hamilton joined Mercedes for 2013, while Horner remained at Red Bull, where Vettel had just secured his third consecutive world championship.

"I listened to his offer and shook my head," Horner wrote. "At that point, Sebastian was at the peak of his powers and Red Bull were in the ascendancy.

"'Niki, I've been winning World Championships with Red Bull,' I said. 'I've built everything from scratch. I feel a loyalty to Dietrich and the team. So as much as I appreciate this, I'm not going to join Mercedes.'"

- Horner: Red Bull blocked moves for Leclerc and Alonso

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How he could shake up Ferrari's future

- How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 title at the US Grand Prix

Mercedes subsequently recruited Wolff from Williams in January 2013, with the Austrian going on to oversee one of the most successful periods in F1 history.

Mercedes won eight consecutive constructors' championships between 2014 and 2021, while Hamilton claimed six drivers' titles with the team.

Horner, meanwhile, remained at Red Bull until his dismissal in July 2025, overseeing four world championships with Vettel and another four with Max Verstappen.

Reflecting on Mercedes' decision to bring Hamilton and Wolff together, Horner admitted he initially underestimated the significance of the partnership.

"Their union was interesting but seemingly inconsequential," he wrote.

"In my mind, I was helping a friend while weakening McLaren, who were our closest rivals at that time. So, what was the worst that could happen?"

Drive, Christian Horner's autobiography, will be released on Oct. 22.

stories.headline: St. Louis City beats Columbus in Open Cup final for club's first trophy
stories.summary: St. Louis City won the first trophy in the club's history on Wednesday after defeating Columbus Crew on penalties to lift the U.S. Open Cup.
stories.body:
Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt made a key save in the penalty shootout of a 120-minute 0-0 tie with the Columbus Crew to help St. Louis City SC win the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup on Wednesday night.

Timo Baumgartl gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead on the first penalty kick and then Lundt dove to his left to get a hand on Santiago Rodriguez's shot that deflected off the post.

St. Louis went 5 for 5 in the shootout, capped by Daniel Edelman's shot down the middle as goalkeeper Nicholas Hagen went the wrong way. Lukas MacNaughton, Chris Durkin and Damion Downs also scored.

St. Louis earned a spot in the 2027 CONCACF Champions Cup after securing the first major trophy in club history.

Columbus was seeking its second U.S. Open Cup title in club history.

Lundt entered the game in the 78th minute after starter Roman Bürki took a knee to the head while making a save. Bürki waved to the crowd while being carted off the field. Lundt came on in relief for his fourth appearance of the season.

It was the first U.S Open Cup final to go to penalties since 2015 when Sporting Kansas City beat the Philadelphia Union. The USOC is open to both professional and amateur clubs, but Major League Soccer teams have dominated the competition for more than two decades.

stories.headline: Retirement doesn't scare Alexander Volkanovski, but neither does fighting at 40
stories.summary: Even at 38 years old, UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski says he will deliver one of the finest performances of his career at UFC 333.
stories.body:
Retirement, for all professional athletes no matter their craft, is inevitable.

But as the next phase of Alexander Volkanovski's life peeks up from beyond the horizon, the UFC featherweight champion says he will deliver a performance at UFC 333 that leaves MMA fans in awe.

"You guys will come out of this being like that's one of Volk's best performances. That's the best way for me to put it," Volkanovski told ESPN after wrapping up a session at the new home of Freestyle MMA.

The gym, which is around 10 times the size of coach Joe Lopez's former premises, is a symbol of the duo's amazing journey from relative MMA obscurity to, at one point, the top of the UFC pound-for-pound rankings.

Volkanovski now sits at No. 7 on ESPN's pound-for-pound chart as he prepares to face undefeated Russian fighter Movsar Evloev, a bout that will be Volkanovski's 33rd professional fight, 12th UFC title fight and 19th in the promotion overall.

"Wow, there you go. It's crazy," Volkanovski said when those numbers were put to him. "It's crazy because even though I know I'm world champion -- or two-time world champion -- I know I was pound-for-pound No. 1, I know I've broken records, but it's weird, it doesn't feel like I've done that much in the UFC. It's hard to explain. It's like, at the end of the day, I do know that I've done it, but I don't live my life thinking I've done that. Does that make sense? It's not even close to a thought of mine.

"I guess it's just because I'm always myself and I just forget about the fighting thing. And I come into the gym and then I've got a job to do and that's that. But then I go back home and then I sort of forget about it all. I don't know why it is that way."

It's that mentality that has endeared Volkanovski to not just Australia, but to fight fans the world over. Just a few weeks on from his 38th birthday, the two-time UFC champion remains as popular as ever.

But having completed another lap around the sun, the questions about his ability to continue compete in arguably the most brutal sport on the earth grow louder than ever.

They just seem to wash right over Volkanovski, however.

"A lot of people will be like, 'F--- this, I'm over this, man. I've had enough.' But I'm still driven," Volkanovski said. "I feel like because I'm driven for these other little things -- other paths to success that still excite me because, I guess, they're different challenges. I'm always trying to challenge myself ... I love the fact that I'm 38 years old. I love the fact that he's [Evloev] undefeated. You name it. I love all these things."

Life outside the Octagon is also vastly different from when Volkanovski first stepped inside the cage.

Now a global sporting star, he has a hugely successful YouTube channel, which includes his "Cooking with Volk" series. He has his own clothing label, and just before flying out to Abu Dhabi for UFC 333, he attended the premiere of the new "Street Fighter" film, in which he plays the role of Joe.

Add to that a small hobby farm that keeps him busy -- he told ESPN that water issues have been plaguing his small cattle herd -- and four young daughters who keep him and wife, Emma, running in all directions.

Retirement no longer scares him. But that doesn't mean he's ready to roll over and accept that his UFC career is done. Volkanovski truly believes he is fighting as well as ever and is fully prepared for whatever Evloev throws at him.

"To fight an undefeated guy, 20-0, never lost in the UFC ... it's cool for [my] legacy. I love it," Volkanovski said.

"I'm going to show him that you know how to win against them other guys, just not me. And that's what I can't wait to go out there and prove. ... A lot of people are like, 'Oh, you know, he's a wrestler' ... but you're not just going to be able to lay on me or hold me down. So that's why now the old dog gets to take out this young guy. You're not hearing people really complain about it. People are excited for this fight, which is pretty cool. I don't need to try and sell it."

With a win in Abu Dhabi, Volkanovski would move to nine featherweight title wins, one clear of José Aldo, though he will have only tied the Brazilian for successful title defences with eight.

There is enough fresh blood at the top of the division to keep Volkanovski busy into 2027, though he has also suggested the idea of a "superfight" for the lightweight title with Justin Gaethje, saying: "Gaethje, Volk. I think he's said that he maybe has one more. That could be a superfight. Let's do a superfight with the lightweight title on the line. We can both see everyone off with a crazy superfight. That could be really good."

However, there is potentially a world in which Volkanovski continues to thwart the best the featherweight division has to offer.

And taking on a title fight beyond his 40th birthday, while unlikely, isn't totally out of the question.

"I can guarantee it won't be 40," Volkanovski said. "I mean, I say that now. It's like, '40, what?' And it's like, 'Mate, it's only two years away.'

"If you ask me that question differently, I'd be like, 'Could you see yourself in two years where I'm like, yeah, yeah, for sure.' But when you say 40, I'm like, 'Nah, I'm not doing 40.' But then here I am at 38. That's two years away. So it could definitely happen, right? But I mean, at the end of the day, none of that will matter. It's going to be how I'm handling things, what damage am I taking?"

What Volkanovski is certain of is that he will deliver a performance against Evloev to rival any from his esteemed UFC career, one that leaves the MMA world in no doubt as to whether he still has what it takes to fight on -- whether he chooses to or not.

"I've said this quite a few times now, that this may be a fight where all you guys are going to be saying that this is probably the best Volk we've ever seen," he told ESPN.

"Do I still believe I'm better than all of them? 100%. But not just that, the fight that this fight's going to bring, and the fight that I'm going to bring, stylistically, you guys will come out of this [saying] that's one of Volk's best performances.

"How, at 38, is Alex pulling off his best f---ing performance? I believe that's what you are going to be saying after this."

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return; Panthers lock in Patea
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Rivals monitor Patea as open market looms
Penrith young gun Luron Patea is expected to test the open market from November 1, with multiple clubs keeping tabs on the promising prop.

Patea is contracted until the end of 2027, but the Panthers are yet to begin talks over an extension, leaving rival clubs poised to explore a deal for 2028 and beyond.

Penrith have not granted Patea permission to negotiate with other clubs before November 1.

The Panthers junior made his NRL debut in 2024 and has shown promise during his first-grade opportunities, providing another emerging option in Penrith's forward pack.

He is among several Panthers players approaching the final year of their contracts, with veteran prop Moses Leota also unsigned beyond 2027.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Try the NBA trade builder: ESPN Analytics' new tool for mock deals
stories.summary: ESPN Analytics is unveiling the NBA Trade Lab, an interactive web application for fans to build, save and vote on mock trades.
stories.body:
Have you ever wanted to build your own projected NBA trade, share it with a friend and have your friend approve -- or deny -- it? Well, now you can do that with thousands of "friends" on ESPN Digital.

ESPN Analytics is unveiling its new NBA Trade Lab, an interactive web application for fans to build, save and vote on mock trades. The tool includes several new features that differentiate it from ESPN's NBA trade machine, including:

• Trade builder: Build, validate and save your own trades in accordance with all current collective bargaining agreement (CBA) rules for other users to vote on. Can you build the perfectly balanced trade that fans of the teams involved would accept?

• Trade swiper: Act as the general manager of your favorite team by voting on trades submitted by other users that involve that team. Swipe right to accept, swipe left to reject.

• Trade viewer: View and filter the full leaderboard of top fan-submitted trades, sorted by highest mutual acceptance rate between all involved teams. Find out the most realistic trade frameworks for your favorite team to acquire the missing player ahead of its playoff push.

Try the NBA Trade Lab now

What you can find within NBA Trade Lab
AUTO-COMPLETE TRADE: Click this button within the trade builder to immediately generate a random trade. It will keep any players or picks already added to the trade and then fill in additional players until it finds a CBA-valid trade. If the trade board is empty, it can also assemble a random trade from scratch.

NET POINTS PROFILES: Click any player card throughout the tool to pop up a view of their net points fingerprint, where you can see each player's overall impact profile broken down across a variety of categories and skills.

MULTITEAM DEALS: When voting in the trade swiper on deals involving three or more teams, the trade view is limited to only what the team you select is sending and receiving. Make the evaluation of complicated multiteam deals much simpler by looking at it from the perspective of each team involved.

ARCHIVED TRADES: Submitted deals get "archived" and moved out of the pool of vote-eligible submissions once they are no longer valid because of subsequent transactions, or when sufficient votes have come in showing that the trade is severely unbalanced.

SALARY CAP & APRON GLOSSARY: At the bottom of the trade builder, you can find a full glossary that explains the definitions of various CBA-related terminology that is used throughout the tool.

FEEDBACK: Find a bug, or a rule that doesn't work? Let us know via the "feedback" button found on the trade builder page.

DATA & DISCLAIMER: Salary and contract data is maintained daily by ESPN Insider Bobby Marks. CBA rules and contracts change, so trade validity also might change.

Mock trades and votes are fan-made, meaning they don't reflect any team's plans or reporting, and no trade shown is a real deal.

stories.headline: Proposing NFL trade deadline offers: Moves for Saquon Barkley, Khalil Mack, more
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley joining a contender? Brian Thomas Jr. headed out west? Khalil Mack and Donte Jackson boosting a defense? Let's build 11 win-win trades.
stories.body:
NFL trade season is about to heat up -- the deadline is less than three weeks away (Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET). We've already seen receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. dealt to the Texans, quarterback J.J. McCarthy moved to the Giants, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sent to the Cowboys and center Cam Jurgens traded to Baltimore. And in the weeks to come, more trades will follow. Let's project some of them with 11 proposals that make sense for both teams involved.

While deadline deals across all sports don't always have a dramatic impact on the games that play out afterward, 2025 was a clear case when moves in the NFL mattered. The Seahawks might not beat the Rams in the regular season without the addition of Rashid Shaheed, who kicked off their comeback victory with a punt return touchdown. That win pushed the Seahawks into position to land the top seed in the NFC, which gave them home-field advantage in the rubber match against the Rams -- and that might have made the difference in the NFC title game. Not a bad return for a pair of Day 3 picks.

Teams with Super Bowl aspirations will be hoping to follow in Seattle's footsteps as the 2026 deadline approaches. If anything, I was a little concerned that there might not be many teams ready to trade away talent, given that 27 of the league's 32 teams still have at least a 9% chance of making it to the postseason after six weeks of football, per ESPN's Football Power Index.

Then two things happened this week to shake up the trade market. One was the firing of Colts general manager Chris Ballard, which came after the Colts blew a 13-0 halftime lead to the Titans at home Sunday and lost 26-20. Ballard endured some unfortunate luck given that his franchise quarterback (Andrew Luck) and one of his best draft picks (Shaquille Leonard) retired prematurely because of serious injuries, but the two big swings Ballard took toward the end of his tenure didn't work out, with QB Anthony Richardson Sr. and cornerback Sauce Gardner both failing to live up to expectations (so far) during their time with the Colts.

Firing Ballard doesn't mean that the Colts are about to trade off every veteran on their roster, especially given that the rest of the front office staff and head coach Shane Steichen still remain, but there's less of a mandate to try to win this season than there would have been with Ballard at the helm. Indy has several pending free agents who could be appealing to opposing teams, and there might be a scenario in which the 2027 version of this franchise has Mannings in the front office and on the football field.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

And then in Philadelphia, we found out that quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season because of deep vein thrombosis. This was already beginning to feel like a lost season for the Eagles, who were missing as many as nine potential starters in Sunday's loss to the Panthers, but the news that Hurts won't be returning anytime soon only reaffirms that the Eagles need to start thinking about 2027. Barring a stunning turn from Tanner McKee, who struggled badly against Carolina, the Eagles don't have any sort of meaningful ceiling this season beyond potentially competing to win a moribund NFC East with a seven- or eight-win season.

This is typically the time of year when GM Howie Roseman calls around on veterans to add to his roster in advance of a playoff push. This season, he's more likely to be the one fielding those calls, and he can't afford to be timid or unrealistic. This Eagles team was flawed even before the Hurts injury. The offensive line, which has long been at the core of so many great Philly teams, has fallen apart. With Lane Johnson retired, Jurgens traded and questions about the future of Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen, the Eagles could need at least two and as many as four new starting linemen next offseason.

They'll also need to work on contracts for young defensive standouts such as Quinyon Mitchell, Jalyx Hunt and Cooper DeJean, which will cause the Eagles to skew far more heavily toward spending on defense after going in the opposite direction. And factoring in the players we already expect not to be back on the roster in 2027, the Eagles could be at $80 million in dead money on next season's cap. Roseman could push money into the future to avoid problems there, but as he did in 2021, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Eagles take a year to reset their cap to create an advantageous situation in 2028 and beyond.

With a need to address multiple spots along the O-line, add depth on defense and potentially line up a long-term replacement for Hurts, Roseman has his work cut out for him over the next 12 months. Adding draft capital would help that process. It wouldn't be a surprise to see the Eagles listen to offers for their pending free agents, and we'll have a trade or two in that direction later in the column. I just wouldn't expect them to move cornerstone players such as Mitchell, DeVonta Smith, Jordan Mailata or Jalen Carter.

I have to start today, though, with a player whose status on the 2027 roster is still up for grabs. Adding him was a masterstroke that elevated the roster and sank the hearts of Philly's division rivals. He was the perfect addition to the team in 2024. But ... is Saquon Barkley going to be on the Eagles in 2027? And if not, would Roseman consider trading his star RB in lieu of losing him for nothing as a cap casualty next offseason?

Barkley was a deserving Offensive Player of the Year candidate in 2024, but he wasn't anywhere near as effective as a runner behind a much worse offensive line in 2025, averaging 4.1 yards per carry (down from 5.8). He has been in and out of the lineup in 2026 because of injuries and turns 30 in February. He's not likely to carry the Eagles very far over the rest of the 2026 season, given that the line is missing multiple starters and the Eagles won't have their starting quarterback the rest of the way.

Barkley is owed $16 million next year, $2.5 million of which is fully guaranteed. That's not an exorbitant sum for a great running back, but I'm not sure the Eagles as constructed in 2027 are going to be in position to get the most out of his talents in the way they were in 2024. Roseman might prefer to use that $16 million to fix what has gone wrong at the line of scrimmage and trust his ability to find a useful back in free agency or in the middle rounds of the draft, as the Eagles did for many years before the Barkley addition.

I wouldn't fault the Eagles for holding on to Barkley, but Roseman won't hesitate to be aggressive if the right deal is out there. And while there aren't a ton of teams in the running back market, there's one that would make sense as a potential Barkley trade partner -- which is where I'll begin our annual list of pre-deadline trade proposals.

Jump to a deal:

MIN-PHI | CAR-PHI | DET-LAC

PIT-LV | SF-IND | LAR-IND

LV-JAX | CHI-TB | NYG-LAC

KC-PHI | NE-WSH

Vikings land an impact RB
Vikings get: RB Saquon Barkley

Eagles get: 2027 third-round pick (with conditions)

At 5-0, the Vikings might very well be the team that's actually in position to benefit from adding a star back in his prime. Minnesota has a 90.9% chance of making it to the postseason, per ESPN's FPI, but it'll need the run game and a healthy back once it gets there. Jordan Mason has already hit injured reserve this season and has battled injuries in each of the past three years. Aaron Jones Sr. is 32 years old, has already left at least one game because of a knee issue and is on pace for 330 carries.

The Vikings are 22nd in explosive play rate on designed runs, which is a reality of life with Jones in the fold. Adding Barkley would allow the Vikings to use him as their primary back while making Jones a complementary player, which is probably the right role for the veteran at this point of his career. Jones can catch passes and block, which would make him an upgrade on DeeJay Dallas, who currently plays that role. Barkley also makes just $867,000 or so over the rest of the season, making him an easy addition for the Vikings financially.

Minnesota would be on the hook for a minimum of $2.5 million next year, although trading a third-round pick for Barkley means the Vikings would probably expect to keep him around in 2027. The Vikings have nearly $38 million in projected cap space next year, a figure that will rise dramatically after a simple restructure of Justin Jefferson's deal, which currently has a $49.4 million cap hold. That figure doesn't include a quarterback, but the Vikings aren't likely to be paying top-level money for their signal-caller next season, especially if they're investing so much in the infrastructure around their starter.

Trading a third-round pick for nearly two years of Barkley at a total cost of about $17 million would be a pretty reasonable bet for the Vikings to make given how well their defense is playing. Jones and Mason could be a solid 1-2 punch, but are you willing to count on them to be present, healthy and productive by the time we get to January? Are the Vikings comfortable using Dallas or Demond Claiborne as their lead backs if not? Barkley isn't the only running back who makes sense for the Vikings, and he has his own injury history to worry about, but he would certainly be the highest-upside option.

In this case, the actual pick the Eagles would land in return would be subject to Barkley's play in Minnesota. The Vikings already own Philly's third-round pick as a result of the Jonathan Greenard trade, and that third-round pick projects to land at the 70th overall slot. Minnesota's own third-round pick projects to fall all the way to No. 93, which is a more dramatic difference than it might seem. Ben Baldwin's draft chart projects the difference between the 70th and 93rd picks as being worth about $6.5 million in surplus value over four years.

So, the terms of this trade: If Barkley runs for 500 or more yards over the remainder of the regular season and the Vikings advance to the playoffs, the Eagles would land the better of the third-round picks (and the lesser if not). If he runs for at least 150 yards in the playoffs and the Vikings advance to the Super Bowl, the pick gets bumped up to a second-rounder.

Trading Barkley would be bittersweet, and Roseman got to see how damaging moving on from him can be to a general manager's reputation from the other side of the coin two years ago. It's also realistic to suggest that Barkley isn't going to be able to play like the guy we saw in 2024 anytime soon in Philadelphia given the lack of infrastructure supporting the run game. If Roseman thinks Barkley is likely to be a cap casualty this offseason, trading him now makes sense. And even if that isn't the case, dealing Barkley for a Day 2 pick and using the cash savings elsewhere next offseason might not necessarily be a bad idea.

Panthers boost their secondary
Panthers get: CB Riq Woolen, 2028 sixth-round pick

Eagles get: TE Ja'Tavion Sanders, 2028 fifth-round pick

Woolen is another veteran who won't be back in Philadelphia next season. Signed to a one-year, $12 million deal to handle outside cornerback duties across from Quinyon Mitchell, Woolen hasn't gotten off to a great start in his new digs, allowing a 109.3 passer rating in coverage. During his time in Seattle, he allowed a 70.6 passer rating in coverage, making a Pro Bowl as a rookie.

While he can be susceptible to double moves and is tied with L'Jarius Sneed for the most penalties committed by a defensive player since the start of 2022, cornerbacks with Woolen's coverage ability and size (6-foot-4) aren't easy to find, especially in the middle of an NFL season. He's going to be best in a zone scheme where he can use that frame to take away throwing lanes on quick routes and make it difficult for quarterbacks to fit passes over the top.

The Panthers are in first place in the NFC South, and while cornerback wasn't a need for them heading into the season, it has become one. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve, leaving Carolina down to Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade at cornerback. The timetable for Horn and Jackson to return isn't clear, so adding a veteran would make plenty of sense. Panthers defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero also runs a scheme similar to Vic Fangio's in Philadelphia, which would make for an easy transition from Woolen's perspective.

It also wouldn't cost Carolina much. Woolen will make just $840,000 plus incentives over the remainder of the season. The Panthers would be giving up a swap of Day 3 picks and a player buried on their depth chart in Sanders, who has been a healthy scratch throughout the 2026 season. Sanders had 33 catches for 342 yards and a touchdown as a rookie in 2024, but he didn't build on that performance in 2025 and hasn't even seen the field in 2026.

With Grant Calcaterra and Dallas Goedert hitting free agency after the season, the Eagles have a hole at tight end. Eli Stowers projects to be the lead option as the move tight end, but Sanders has the size to play as a more traditional option and the athleticism to create after the catch. He won't turn 24 until March, is owed just $1.9 million combined over the next two years and can play on special teams, which would make Sanders a reasonable second or (preferably) third tight end option for the Eagles as they rebuild that room.

Lions attack their defensive flaws
Lions get: Edge Khalil Mack, CB Donte Jackson

Chargers get: 2027 fourth- and sixth-round picks

One of the few teams that is very obviously out of the playoff picture, the 0-6 Chargers are staring down a lost season. They're not about to tear down the roster given that Justin Herbert is still only 28 years old, but GM Joe Hortiz also finds himself in a position to move on from veterans who aren't likely to be on the roster in 2028 and beyond.

Jackson fits that bill. The well-traveled cornerback played at a Pro Bowl level last season after going to the Chargers from the Steelers, making him one of many defensive backs to produce career years after joining up with Jesse Minter (who might very well be interested in adding him to play on the outside in Baltimore). This year, though, Jackson has been limited to 113 snaps by hamstring issues.

Mack, who was considering retirement before returning to the Chargers on a one-year deal, would also be an obvious trade candidate. At 35 years old, he is still a valuable edge defender for the Chargers. He has three sacks and six quarterback knockdowns through six games, and Mack's 5.0% quick pressure rate is still well above the league average of 3.9%. Mack has always been solid against the run, and he can step into any defense and be a viable, above-average edge rusher for the remainder of the season if he can stay healthy.

Both players are free agents after the season, and there's a decent amount of money involved here. Jackson is owed $4 million over the remainder of the season, while Mack is due $5.3 million. NFL teams don't necessarily need to cut payroll in a lost season, but the Chargers wouldn't mind adding draft capital for two players who might not be back next seasons, especially if they can save millions of dollars in the process. They could alternately want to eat some of that money to add more draft capital in a potential trade and think the picks are a better use of the cash than players who would be playing out the string for a hopeless team.

Guess who could use an edge rusher and a cornerback? The Lions. DJ Wonnum has a team-high five sacks as he takes advantage of defenses double-teaming Aidan Hutchinson, but Detroit could certainly use another edge rusher to take some of the workload off its two starters and provide some help if Hutchinson or Wonnum go down. And the Lions are incredibly desperate for cornerback help, given that they're relying on the likes of Ennis Rakestraw Jr., Rock Ya-Sin and Roger McCreary for meaningful snaps this season. Jackson would be a cut above those players and a viable second option alongside D.J. Reed, who has also struggled so far this season.

In this deal, the Chargers eat about half of the money owed to Jackson and Mack over the remainder of the season, making the midseason cash expenditure more palatable for the Lions. The Lions have the league's second-best offense in terms of points scored per drive, but the defense needs help. And here Detroit adds two experienced starters on that side of the ball, giving the team a better shot at competing in what's going to be a dogfight in the NFC North.

Steelers bring in a veteran on the back end
Steelers get: S Isaiah Pola-Mao, 2028 seventh-round pick

Raiders get: 2028 sixth-round pick

Here's another defensive back with a realistic shot of being moved before the deadline. Pola-Mao started at free safety for the Raiders in 2024 and 2025 under then-coordinator Patrick Graham. The Raiders signed the homegrown starter to a two-year, $7.6 million extension before the 2026 season, but second-round pick Treydan Stukes won the starting job in camp, and the Raiders don't play many three-safety looks. Pola-Mao has played just 112 snaps this season, almost all of which came while Stukes missed part of Week 2 and all of Week 3 because of a concussion.

Pola-Mao isn't a great player, but he's a viable safety in a pinch. And the Steelers seem to be in a pinch for safety help around this time every year. This time around, the organization quickly lost faith in veteran Rayshawn Jenkins, who has been on the scene of the crime for multiple disasters this season. Against the Browns, he missed a tackle on a Jaleel McLaughlin touchdown run, then appeared to rotate to the wrong side of the field on a 60-yard completion to Denzel Boston. He was benched shortly thereafter, didn't play a defensive snap over the two ensuing weeks and was released Wednesday.

The Steelers are using Jaquan Brisker and rookie seventh-round pick Robert Spears-Jennings at safety, with Jalen Ramsey playing in a hybrid slot/safety role. Brisker's injury history and Spears-Jennings' inexperience would suggest that the Steelers would be wise to at least add a veteran safety as depth. Trading Pola-Mao would save the Raiders $2.4 million over the remainder of 2026, a worthwhile amount for a team that doesn't see the fifth-year undrafted free agent as part of its future plans.

49ers add a run stopper
49ers get: DT Grover Stewart, 2027 seventh-round pick

Colts get: 2027 sixth-round pick

San Francisco fans are understandably dreaming about a reunion with DeForest Buckner, who was once dealt in the opposite direction between these two teams for a first-round pick, but I'm not sure that's as great of a fit as it might seem. The 49ers already have Osa Odighizuwa playing in that penetrating defensive tackle role, and rookie Gracen Halton has flashed alongside him, with sacks in each of the past two games.

Buckner is still a great player, and I wouldn't fault the 49ers for just lining up as many superstars up front as possible and daring opposing offensive lines to simply figure it out, but this team really needs more help at nose tackle. The 49ers are 27th in success rate against the run so far this season. A year ago, they were 31st. The 49ers have been able to insulate themselves against run game issues by playing from ahead for most of the season, but they'll need to be better against the run by the postseason.

Adding Stewart to the defensive line rotation would go a long way in helping the 49ers plug up those run game woes. The 33-year-old is a useful player and in the final year of his deal, but his contract is also expensive; he's owed $8.2 million in cash over the remainder of the season. The 49ers don't have cap concerns after restructuring some of their more significant deals, but that's a big cash outlay. They could encourage the Colts to absorb more of the money by offering a better draft pick, but with the 49ers still undefeated and fielding one of the oldest cores in football, I'd push ownership to spend now to try to build a team that can win a title. Stewart isn't the most exciting addition, but he's the sort of player the Niners need.

Rams fix their kicking game
Rams get: K Spencer Shrader

Colts get: 2027 fifth-round pick

In a crowded NFC West race, the Rams might look to throw draft capital at their kicking woes. Sean McVay is already on his third kicker of the season after cutting Harrison Mevis and losing Blake Grupe to injured reserve. The Rams just signed veteran Brandon McManus as a stopgap, but McManus missed three kicks in Green Bay's wild-card-round loss to Chicago last season.

Does McVay really want to go down that route? One solution would be trying to find a long-term option. Shrader bounced around the league early in his career, but he has found a home in Indianapolis. Over his career, the 27-year-old has gone 36-of-37 on field goals and 35-for-36 on extra points, including 6-for-6 on field goals over 50-plus yards this season.

Playing his home games in a dome obviously helps, but Shrader is one of the league's most accurate kickers, and he won't be an unrestricted free agent until 2028. He is a useful player for the Colts, but he's also not an essential piece for a team that's rebuilding. And having dealt two first-round picks to the Jets for Sauce Gardner, Indy could use all the draft capital it can get.

Raiders get an offensive playmaker
Raiders get: WR Brian Thomas Jr.

Jaguars get: 2027 second-round pick

After months of denying that they were interested in trading Thomas, the Jaguars might have finally come to a breaking point with their former top wide receiver. Thomas caught zero passes during Jacksonville's two-game road trip in London. In the win over the Eagles, he wasn't able to get his feet down in the corner of the end zone for what could have been a touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. Then against the Texans, Thomas dropped an admittedly low throw from Lawrence that might have set the Jaguars up for a long field goal attempt just before halftime.

Thomas didn't play a single snap in the second half of the loss to the Texans, and afterward, coach Liam Coen didn't hide his frustration. "Guys have to make plays," Coen said about the 2024 first-round pick. Travis Hunter, who played his largest offensive role of the season, made some of those plays in Thomas' absence. With the Jags committed to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers as starters, rookie Josh Cameron earning a larger piece of the rotation, Hunter's role potentially expanding and the Jags wanting to play 12 personnel to get Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher on the field, there's just not a big role for Thomas at the moment.

The Marvin Harrison Jr. trade established an asking price for Thomas. Harrison was a better prospect entering the league in the same draft class, which would make him more appealing to teams that really value their scouting reports. Thomas, on the other hand, has actually had a high-end season as a pro, racking up 1,282 yards as a rookie while catching passes from Lawrence and Mac Jones. I'm not sure there were a lot of teams lining up to trade a second-round pick for Harrison, but the Cardinals were able to find one. I expect that the Jaguars could also find one here.

And at the right price, there should be a lot of teams willing to take a shot on Thomas, who has legitimate high-end speed and the ability to separate from man coverage. The Rams, who have pillaged Jacksonville for young players in the past, could very well see Thomas as a value addition and both a short- and long-term replacement for Davante Adams, who is out for two months and a free agent after the year.

The most obvious candidate for a Thomas trade, though, would be the Raiders. Vegas still needs to add receiver help beyond tight end Brock Bowers for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Tre Tucker has been effective as a deep threat, but he's probably stretched as a primary wide receiver and will be a free agent after the season. Offseason addition Jalen Nailor, signed to a three-year, $35 million deal, has six catches in five games. Bowers is brilliant, and Michael Mayer has been a valuable in-line tight end, but coach Klint Kubiak needs a receiver who can both stretch the defense and run a full route tree.

The Raiders' playoff chances are sub-10%, per the FPI, and barring a significant winning streak, they're not really in a place to add a short-term option for 2026. Thomas would be more of a long-term addition. He's owed $3.5 million combined over the next two years and would have a fifth-year option available for $17.2 million in 2028. At $7 million per year over the next three seasons, Thomas would be making No. 3 receiver money for the Raiders with the upside to be a potential lead option.

Is there a risk in trading a second-round pick for a wide receiver who is frustrating the team that drafted him? Of course. The Bears traded a second-round pick for Chase Claypool, who was falling down the depth chart in Pittsburgh, and got 18 catches over two years from him before moving on. The Steelers used the pick they landed for Claypool -- which ended up being the top selection of the second round -- to draft Joey Porter Jr. The Raiders aren't likely to completely collapse over the rest of the season, but there's a chance that they end up sending a pick toward the top of the second round to the Jaguars for Thomas. Of course, the chance to add a potential star wideout for the quarterback-in-waiting also seems like a worthwhile risk to take.

Bears find some edge-rush support
Bears get: Edge Anthony Nelson, 2027 seventh-round pick

Buccaneers get: 2027 sixth-round pick

Speaking of the Bears, let's get them some extra depth on the edge. The Bears actually have a 9.8% sack rate when they rush four or fewer this season, one of the best rates in the NFL, but they're operating somewhere below 100%. Dayo Odeyingbo is on injured reserve, and Montez Sweat is serving a two-game suspension for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing drugs. Both will be back sooner rather than later, but nobody has ever gotten to the postseason and complained about having too many pass rushers.

Nelson represents reasonable depth behind Odeyingbo, Sweat and Austin Booker, who leads the Bears with four sacks. Nelson has been a rotational player for most of his time with Tampa Bay, but the signing of Al-Quadin Muhammad, the selection of Rueben Bain Jr. in the first round of this year's draft and the surprising emergence of second-year pro David Walker has kept Nelson off the field. The 29-year-old has played just 12 of 139 possible defensive snaps over the past two weeks for the 1-5 Bucs.

In addition, Nelson will make about $2.7 million over the rest of the season, which isn't going to be very appealing to the Bucs if he's taking most of his snaps on special teams. A competitive Bears team could integrate Nelson into the roster as the fourth edge rusher on game days. Bears fans might want someone like Josh Sweat, and I can understand why, but Chicago's pass rush has quietly been more effective than many expected heading into the season, which leads me to a more modest addition up front.

Giants address their thin interior
Giants get: DT Dalvin Tomlinson, 2028 seventh-round pick

Chargers get: 2028 sixth-round pick

Another veteran reserve for the Chargers who could be on the move between now and the deadline, Tomlinson would be coming full circle after starting his career in New York. The well-traveled defensive tackle isn't the interior disruptor we saw earlier in his career, but Tomlinson is also only two years removed from an 18-knockdown season with the Browns in 2024. He's a pending free agent with the Chargers and due $2.1 million over the rest of 2026.

The Giants started the season thin on the interior after trading away Dexter Lawrence II and losing Roy Robertson-Harris to a torn Achilles. They've gotten by through adding veterans such as Shelby Harris and DJ Reader, and Tomlinson would be another defensive tackle in that vein. The only Giants DT with a sack this season is CJ Okoye, so even a modest contribution from Tomlinson while playing about 35-40% of the defensive snaps would go a long way.

Chiefs think about the long and short term
Chiefs get: TE Dallas Goedert

Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick

There has been talk about the Chiefs adding Tyreek Hill or another wide receiver as a replacement for the injured Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton, and it's entirely possible that they add a wideout at some point before the end of the season. With the Chiefs playing bullyball and building their offense around Kenneth Walker III, though, I wonder whether going in the opposite direction might be a better idea. They already use 12 or 13 personnel on nearly 40% of Patrick Mahomes' dropbacks. So, what about adding another receiving tight end to the mix?

Here, Chiefs coach Andy Reid goes back to his old employers to add a versatile playmaker in Goedert, who scored a career-high 11 touchdowns a season ago as one of the few players who seemed to thrive under offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo. Goedert is most efficient as a receiver out of the slot, but he can also work inline as a blocker or pass catcher, too. He would give the Chiefs some leverage against the possibility of Travis Kelce slowing down as the season goes along and work alongside the future Hall of Famer as a potential mismatch over the middle of the field.

Goedert will make just $870,000 over the remainder of the season, so the Chiefs won't have any financial trouble fitting him onto their roster. The longtime Eagles standout is a free agent after the season, and he's likely to be replaced in the long term by rookie second-round pick Eli Stowers, who began the season on injured reserve. Chiefs GM Brett Veach might be reticent to trade draft picks for short-term options after moves for players such as DeAndre Hopkins haven't necessarily paid off in recent years, but Goedert could also be the replacement for Kelce as the primary tight end in Kansas City if he signs a new deal after the season.

Patriots pad their OL depth
Patriots get: OL Andrew Wylie, 2027 seventh-round pick

Commanders get: 2027 sixth-round pick

It's rare to see a team nearly run out of linemen in an NFL game, but the Patriots came close last week. With Mike Onwenu already sidelined and Will Campbell playing despite a knee injury, the Patriots lost Alijah Vera-Tucker, Morgan Moses and Ben Brown during a win over the Jets, leaving the defending AFC champs with a mere five healthy offensive linemen. The line made it through the rest of the contest, and Moses could be back this week, but the Patriots are remarkably thin up front.

Adding a versatile lineman to the mix makes a lot of sense. Wylie can play right tackle or either guard spot, allowing him to fill in across the lineup with relative ease. He's buried on the Commanders' depth chart and has played just 15 snaps this season despite the absence of left tackle Laremy Tunsil, which caused Brandon Coleman to move to the left side.

With multiple sixth-round picks, the Patriots can afford to ship one off to add a veteran. And the Commanders could turn to practice-squaders Trent Scott or Esa Pole, who filled in for the Chiefs at left tackle last season, as their swing tackle after Wylie's departure.

stories.headline: Frank Leboeuf blasts Bruno Fernandes for 'betrayal': 'Start running and stop talking'
stories.summary: France legend Frank Leboeuf has slammed Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes for his criticism of Michael Carrick following the club's after a humiliating 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.
stories.body:
Frank Leboeuf has slammed Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes for his criticism of head coach Michael Carrick following the club's after a 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

Fernandes appeared to directly question Carrick's tactics, as he said: "It was a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind."

Carrick responded to his captain's comments and said: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."

Former Chelsea centre-back Leboeuf, speaking on ESPN FC, had strong words for Fernandes and his United teammates.

"We witnessed a betrayal. A betrayal towards the coach, towards the fans and towards the club from the players," Leboeuf said. "We have to blame the players. We have to make them guilty for what we see.

"You can talk about the tactic, maybe it wasn't the best tactic. But maybe Michael Carrick knows too much about the players and what they're incapable of doing. It's why he was maybe a little bit too defensive ... Those players, they're letting him down," he added.

"They don't run for him. They don't run for the club, they don't give 100%. And Bruno Fernandes ... That guy, what I see too much is cheating, crying, complaining. Yes, he's a great player but start running, stop talking!

"After Lisandro Martínez, some players talk too much. Just do your job. Try to do your job for the club, for the fans, for the players. You are not there. You are absolutely invisible.

"That was awful and appalling because the players didn't do the job."

Another former Chelsea player, and former England midifielder, Joe Cole also weighed in on Fernandes' remarks and slammed the United captain.

"[He's] absolutely questioning the tactics," Cole said. "It doesn't matter whether he is right to. That's sacrilege.

"I've played for managers where I don't agree with the tactics. You might say that to your mate or your wife, but you don't come out as captain of the club and question the manager.

"He doesn't even do it properly. If you're going to come out, be bold, and say it with your chest. He sort of says, 'we could have been this, but then it's up to the manager.'

- Man United players were abysmal in Como, but it's Carrick who faces consequences

- Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes criticism after Man United loss at Como

- Champions League talking points: What to make of the Man Utd mess

"He probably thinks he's clever, [like saying] 'well, I didn't really say it, gaffer.' You said what you said, you thought they got the tactics wrong. You can think that, that's fine," he added.

"You can go into the manager's office tomorrow, and say, 'I think you got it wrong, gaffer.' Have a man-to-man conversation.

"To come out in front of the nation, when you're captain of the football club, and question the manager is simply unacceptable.

"Bruno has really got that wrong. If you're captain of Manchester United, you cannot come out and question the tactics. It would not have happened under Sir Alex Ferguson."

The defeat at Como means that United are winless in their last seven games across all competitions. They have won just two of the 11 games they have played so far this season.

Next up, they will host Bournemouth in the Premier League on Sunday.
